answer.line: First-order half-life is 0.693 / k, whatever amount you start with: 0.693 / 0.0693 = 10 min.

steps: Name the order first. First order means the half-life is 0.693 / k, with no starting amount in it.
Divide: 0.693 / 0.0693 = 10. The digits match, so it is a clean factor of ten.
Picture it: every 10 minutes, half of what is left is gone. 1, then 1/2, then 1/4.

choices.note: 2 / 0.0693 is about 28.9. Half-life carries ln 2, which is 0.693, not 2.
0.0693 / 0.693 = 0.1 flips the fraction. A bigger k means a faster reaction and a shorter half-life, so k goes underneath.
1 / k = 14.4 min is a real time, where about 37 percent is left. Half is gone sooner, at 0.693 / k.
0.693 x 0.0693 = 0.048 multiplies where it should divide. A slow k cannot give a half-life of seconds.

lockIt: First order: half-life = 0.693 / k, the same from any starting amount.
